Third-party claim: what to do when it's not your fault

Four quick screens. Tap your answer, then Next.

Are you hurt? Do you need a tow?

Call 995 for an ambulance now. When someone is hurt, the Police must also be told.

Stay out of the traffic lane and get a tow.

Good. Collect the details on the next screen before anyone leaves.

995 Ambulance999 PoliceTow truck

Collect these before anyone leaves

  • The other driver's name and contact number
  • Their plate number
  • Their insurer's name
  • Photos of both cars, the plates and the scene
  • Witness names and contacts
  • Any in-car camera footage (save it now)

You must still report to your own insurer

The GIA Motor Claims Framework says: report the accident to your insurer within 24 hours or by the next working day. Take your vehicle, damaged or not, to your insurer's approved reporting centre or authorised workshop.

This applies even when the other driver is at fault.

Questions people ask

What is a third-party claim?

When another driver caused the accident, you claim your repair costs and other losses from that driver's insurer instead of your own policy.

Do I still need to report to my own insurer if it's not my fault?

Yes. Report to your own insurer within 24 hours or by the next working day, even when you claim from the other driver's insurer.

What details should I get from the other driver?

Their name, contact number, plate number and insurer, plus photos of both cars and the scene, and contacts of any witnesses.
